Delay `updateAll()` & only update subset immediately (#815)

* Delay `updateAll()` & only update subset immediately

If the number of peers is greater than or equal to `MIN_PEER_UPDATE_ALL`
(currently `10`), only a subset of the peers are scanned immediately.
A full scan is schedule later with a delay based on the number of peers.
`Math.sqrt(this.peers.length) * 100ms`

`updateAll()` now takes an optional `limit` arg so the code is reused
between the subset & complete scans.

All calls to `updateAll()` were refactor to `queueUpdateAll()` except in
`core.truncate()` as that is assumed to be strongly propagated.

Add mutex to MarkBitfield write batch (#863)

Without this mutex setting a series of bits synchronously can race on
which wins. `markBlock - range` would flake because of this with the
last set to flush being the index `2` which is last because it loads the
bitfield page in order to create it. `2`'s bitfield write was the
correct final bitfield but lost to another write.

Skip errors when replicator destroyed (#861)

* Use replicator destroy instead of core closing

Using the replicator state instead of the core is a closer layer to
reference and is more reflective of "no more io" at the replication
layer. The replicator is always destroyed before the db layer is closed
so covers the same errors from the db.

* Ignore errors from flushing hints if replicator is destroyed

Removed the core.closing check as it should never be hit since the
replicator will close the channel preventing any more range requests.
But the IO to disk to update the hints could throw. So put in a try
catch, skip if replicator is destroyed otherwise rethrow.

* Dont destroy stream with error if replicator already destroyed

* Skip pushing node if replicator is destroyed

Same as existing guard, but using replicator instead since a destroyed
replicator shouldnt be able to push blocks.

* Ignore errors when handling request if replicator is destroyed

The guard for handling queued requests likely doesn't help since the
channels are closed when the core is closed. There is a guard for the
`.removed` flag and the receiverQueue is cleared on closing the peer.

The IO for disk however can trigger an error. So errors catch are
ignored if the replicator is destroyed.

* Bail early if replicator destroyed before fulfilling request

* Clarify db closing for closing replicator pending IO test

Explicitly closing the db isn't required to trigger the errors as
closing the core is enough to close the storage. To ensure the storage
is closed, the db.close is moved into a teardown hook.

* Move test for post closing replicator message errors above helpers

* Revert guards by relying on `protomux` warning to catch errors

* Add test for emitting `warning` on error after channel closed

* Warn via protomux internal `_warn()` when `_send` throws w/o replicator

`_send()` is a promise but is never caught and is use many places.
Errors previously propagated via `this.stream.destroy()` but we
explicitly don't want the stream to destroy when the channel or the
replicator is closed.

The fact that an error occurred shouldn't be swallowed so a compromise
is to use the new protomux `_warn()` method as though it was another
handler error (`onopen`, `onmessage` etc).

* Remove trailing new line in `test/replicate.js`

* Update guard in `_send()` to use `.removed`

This way it doesn't rely on the replicator being destroyed and is more
specifically if the current peer's channel is closed.

* Drop error if channel is closed in `_send()`

* Update 'wire messages arriving...' test to reflect dropping warning
